minutes.headline: Capital Planning Committee reorganized and began redesigning its five-year capital planning process; no budget votes were taken.
minutes.summary: The committee, down to four members with a vacancy, elected a new chair, vice chair and clerk after the chair said he could not continue. Most of the meeting discussed how to run a five-year capital plan alongside the FY26 cycle: standardized templates, scoring, funding-source lenses, department timing and the Brooks House. Next steps were set for a standards proposal and a draft calendar, and a next meeting date was agreed.

attendees.role: member addressed by the chair (also speaks in public comment)

public_comment.topic: Urged the Board of Selectmen to apply remaining ARPA funds to small infrastructure projects on the capital list: leaking DPW garage, Boys and Girls Club, public safety building second-floor engineering.

Asked for broader community equity in capital priorities (playground, senior center parking), continuity of funded projects (town beach and Marshall Pond permit, the 2010 parking lot design money) and consistent criteria.
Said the five-year plans will reveal needs beyond available revenue and that an override will be needed within the next two years.

votes.motion: Nominate Tom Alonzo as vice chair

budget_items.what_was_said: A resident asked that remaining ARPA money go to small capital projects; committee members agreed that smaller envelope projects make sense.
Members said the capital review should consider Chapter 90, grants and other small funds, not only the omnibus budget and free cash.
A member noted timing of matching MSBA money must be planned for school building projects.
Members discussed whether an impervious surface fee or another source should fund drainage, and that no dedicated fund exists for culverts and bridges.
The gap between funds projected for capital and the five-year requests was described as large.
Funding was received for the Turkey Hill assessment and design work, which adds to department workload.

budget_items.topic: Town beach and Marshall Pond permit; Council on Aging parking lot
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident cited a prior appropriation for a permit not followed by treatment funding and an old design appropriation for the parking lot.
A resident said revenue needs will require an override.

decisions.decision: Peter beer was put forward as chair and Tom Alonzo as vice chair; the captions show the voice calls but not results.

Chair will bring a proposed plan on information, standardized presentations and data collection (Excel template, scoring examples) to the next meeting, and work from the town manager's draft budget calendar.
Next meeting set for Monday July 29 at 7 p.m., preferably in the lower room with the owl camera.
Schools asked to submit capital requests in summer or September rather than October, because of Turkey Hill work.

A clerk was also to be appointed, but that vote is not audible in the captions, so no outcome can be stated.
Members discussed running a five-year capital plan alongside the next budget cycle, including templates, scoring, funding sources, stormwater and school building timing.
The chair is to bring a proposed plan on standardized information and data collection to the next meeting, working from the town manager's draft budget calendar.
The next meeting was set for Monday, July 29, at 7 p.m.; no budget votes were taken.

why_it_matters: The committee reviews the town's capital requests, so how it scores projects and sorts funding sources shapes which buildings, drainage and school projects reach a Town Meeting vote.
Residents raised small projects funded from leftover ARPA money and a possible override within two years; neither was decided, and the committee has not yet set its process.
